messages.content: Write a post about what a software company learned from a year of remote work. Around 250 words.

output:
**A year of remote: what we got wrong**

We closed the office last March. Not as an experiment — the lease ended and nobody argued to renew it.

Meetings didn't go away. They mutated. Calendar load went from 11 hours a week per engineer to 16 by June, because every hallway question turned into a 30-minute call, that being the only shape the calendar offered. We made 15 minutes the default block and killed the recurring status meeting outright. Standup is a thread now.

Onboarding broke first and loudest. Two of our four hires that year said they didn't feel useful until month four. The old apprenticeship — sit near someone, absorb by overhearing — has no remote version, and pairing over video isn't it. What worked: give each new hire a bug on day two that touches three services, and one named person whose job is answering dumb questions within the hour.

Writing got better because it had to. Design docs went from optional to load-bearing. That's the change we'd keep even if everyone walked back into an office tomorrow.

The thing we still can't solve is disagreement. Hard conversations over video end early and politely, and then the real argument continues in DMs where nobody else can see it. So we fly the whole team in for three days a quarter, and we spend those days on the arguments rather than the demos.

Flights cost us $48k last year. The lease was $210k.

---

245 words, saved at `/tmp/remote_post.md`. The numbers are invented placeholders — swap in your real calendar data, headcount, and lease figures, since the specifics are what keep it from reading like every other remote-work retrospective.
